title: Lavash baking
summary: In Armenia, lavash is a very thin flatbread. The baker stretches rested dough over a cushion, presses it on the hot clay wall of a sunken oven called a tonir, and lifts it out on a hook when it is blistered and golden.
howToPlay: Stretch: drag over the dough on the cushion in steady passes to thin it evenly. Going too fast tears it.
Stick: press To the oven, then press on the wall and hold; let go inside the lit part of the bar so the sheet clings.
Bake: the wall is hotter low and on the fire side. Sheets blister and brown, and thin places colour first.
Lift: tap a sheet to hook it off when it is golden. Pale is raw, dark is lost.
rules: A sheet is scored on how thin and even it is, how cleanly it stuck, and its colour when lifted.
The round score is the mean of the sheets in the order.
A sheet that falls or burns scores nothing.
heritageNote: Lavash belongs to the everyday food culture of Armenia and its neighbours. Bakers, often women of a village working together, lean into the warm pit to press the dough on the wall and stack the sheets to keep for the week.
